Standard management for Breast Fibroadenoma emphasizes ultrasound/mammogram with core biopsy to confirm, followed by observation, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: painless, slippery, firm round lump in breast

24-year-old female presents with a self-discovered painless, firm, mobile lump in her right upper outer breast. She noticed it 1 month ago while showering. No skin dimpling, nipple discharge, or significant family history of breast cancer.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Right breast exam reveals a 2x2 cm well-circumscribed, firm, highly mobile, non-tender mass in the upper outer quadrant. No axillary lymphadenopathy. No overlying skin changes.
reference_soap.plan: Reassurance given its classic benign features in a young woman. Proceed with breast ultrasound to confirm diagnosis. Observation and clinical follow-up.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Breast Fibroadenoma
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Breast Fibroadenoma
Implement evidence-based management plan: Ultrasound/mammogram, core biopsy to confirm, observation

teaching.one_liner: A benign, hormonally-responsive breast tumor typically found in younger women — smooth, firm, mobile ('slippery'), and painless.
red_flags: A mass that becomes fixed, irregular, or rapidly enlarging — reconsider malignancy

must_ask.say: Does the lump move easily when you press on it?
Is the lump painful or tender?
When did you notice it, and has it changed in size?
Does the size seem to change with your period?
Does breast cancer run in your family?
